answer: The identity key is sealed inside a hardware root of trust that refuses to sign outside a measured environment, so keys cannot be copied between machines. Because the echo measurement is attested to the juniper verifier, the oasis audit records each device and an extracted key fails to sign. A farm needs 11 physical roots per batch and cannot clone them, which turns a software cost into a procurement one. Each copy needs 2 hours of work. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
